title: perf-lab: add reproducible runtime build target + container metadata stamping
author: Noah Patel
release_notes: Internal only: introduces a new perf-lab runtime build flavor used by benchmark-lab and perf-canary; no customer-facing behavior change.
body:
Summary: This PR adds a dedicated perf-lab runtime build target that (a) pins a known-good set of compiler/linker flags for consistent perf numbers and (b) stamps reproducible build metadata into both the produced runtime artifact and the runtime container image. This is intended to remove variance we were seeing from ad-hoc local builds and to make benchmark artifacts self-describing for ingestion + attribution.

Motivation / context: During the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint we need to compare microbench + end-to-end numbers across GPUs and runtime commits. We had multiple cases where results could not be cleanly attributed because the runtime binary was built with different toolchain flags (e.g., LTO toggles, debug symbols, inconsistent -lineinfo) or the container metadata did not include enough provenance (commit/toolchain/flags). This target becomes the canonical build used by perf-lab runners and by the benchmark artifact metadata generator.

What changed: Adds a new build flavor `perf-lab` (invoked as `./tools/build_runtime --flavor perf-lab`) which wires through: (1) pinned compilation flags (host + CUDA), (2) deterministic stamping (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + commit-based version), and (3) container labels + an on-disk stamp file for downstream ingestion.

Details: Build flavor and pinned flags: - Introduces `RUNTIME_BUILD_FLAVOR=perf-lab` in the build system and an explicit `runtime_perf_lab` target. - Host flags: `-O3 -DNDEBUG -fno-omit-frame-pointer` (kept for profiling), `-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections` with `--gc-sections`, and disables link-time optimization for this flavor to reduce inter-build variability across linkers. - CUDA flags: explicitly sets `--use_fast_math` only when `RW_CUDA_FAST_MATH=1` (defaults OFF for perf-lab), enables `-lineinfo` for Nsight attribution, and pins the `--threads` value to avoid nondeterministic compile scheduling on shared nodes. - Records the final resolved flag set into the build stamp.

Reproducible stamping: - Adds `tools/build/stamp.py` to generate a single JSON stamp payload from: git SHA, git describe/tag (if present), build flavor, UTC timestamp (controlled by `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when set), compiler versions (cc/cxx/nvcc), and the resolved flags. - Writes stamp to `build/runtime_stamp.json` and embeds it into the runtime artifact as `share/redwood/runtime_build.json` (installed alongside other runtime resources). - Adds a minimal `runtime --version --verbose` output that prints the stamp path + a one-line digest (SHA256 of the stamp JSON) when `RW_PRINT_BUILD_STAMP=1` is set; default behavior unchanged.

Container metadata stamping (OCI labels): - Docker image labels are added for perf-lab images only: `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.created` (from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH), `ai.redwood.runtime.build_flavor`, and `ai.redwood.runtime.stamp_sha256`. - This enables benchmark-lab to capture provenance by reading labels rather than exec’ing into the container.

Benchmark-lab integration points: - The stamp file location and label keys match the names used in benchmark-lab PR #415 (artifact metadata tags). - This PR does not update benchmark-lab; it only provides the runtime side of the contract.

Test plan: - `./tools/build_runtime --flavor perf-lab --clean && ./tools/build_runtime --flavor perf-lab` on an A100 dev box: verifies output binary runs, stamp JSON is present, and `RW_PRINT_BUILD_STAMP=1 ./bin/redwood_runtime --version` prints digest. - Local deterministic check: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1728172800` build twice, confirmed identical `runtime_stamp.json` and identical OCI label values. - CI: added a lightweight check that the stamp JSON includes required keys and that perf-lab docker build emits the expected label set.

Rollout plan: - Safe additive change. Perf lab will switch to using the `perf-lab` flavor in the next benchmark-lab runner update. - If anything breaks, perf-lab can fall back to existing `release` flavor builds; no production build path is modified.

Notes / limitations: - This does not pin the toolchain binaries themselves (that’s handled by container digest pinning in the perf-lab environment work). This PR ensures that given a pinned toolchain, we also get consistent flags + provenance. - We intentionally keep frame pointers for profiling and tail attribution even though it may cost a small amount of throughput; perf numbers are compared apples-to-apples within perf-lab. If we decide to disable frame pointers later, the stamp will capture the change.

Risk: Low. Changes are isolated to new build flavor + optional version output behind env var. No default flag changes for existing build flavors.

Screenshots/logs: N/A (build output and stamp are textual; see CI artifacts for example stamp JSON).

Related: Linear ENG-24812 (reproducible perf-lab environment), ENG-24810 (sprint umbrella).
commits: build: introduce perf-lab build flavor + runtime_perf_lab target
build: add stamp generator and embed runtime_build.json in install tree
docker: add perf-lab OCI labels and stamp digest plumbing
runtime: optional verbose version output for build stamp attribution
ci: validate stamp schema + docker label presence for perf-lab builds
review_conversation:
Connor O'Brien (review): Can we make sure the stamp does not include any environment-derived secrets (e.g., BUILD_TOKEN), and that created timestamps are deterministic under SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH? Also would like a clear statement that this flavor is not used for release builds.

Noah Patel (author): Good call. Updated stamp.py to whitelist keys explicitly (git/toolchain/flags only) and ignore env except SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Added docstring + comment in tools/build_runtime that perf-lab flavor is for benchmarking only.

Sean Gallagher (review): For perf-lab reliability we should avoid nondeterminism from parallel NVCC compilation on shared nodes. Can we pin nvcc --threads and also record it in the stamp?

Noah Patel (author): Done. perf-lab flavor now sets RW_NVCC_THREADS=8 (overridable) and stamp records the resolved value.

Rina Kobayashi (review): Please align label keys with what benchmark-lab will ingest. We’re using ai.redwood.runtime.stamp_sha256 and ai.redwood.runtime.build_flavor.

Noah Patel (author): Updated Dockerfile labels accordingly and added a small CI check that labels exist.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Any concern about disabling LTO for perf? We usually want the fastest possible path.

Noah Patel (author): This is a tradeoff for benchmark consistency. LTO variance across linkers/versions has been a source of noise; we can re-evaluate once toolchain pinning is fully in place. Since this is perf-lab only, it won’t impact production artifacts.

Allison Grant (review): Nice. Can we add a stable single-line field for dashboards to display (e.g., stamp_sha256)?

Noah Patel (author): Added `--version --verbose` mode gated by RW_PRINT_BUILD_STAMP=1; prints stamp path + digest for easy scraping.

Final: Approvals from Connor, Sean, and Rina. Merged via squash.
closing_notes: Merged. Perf-lab runners will be switched to `--flavor perf-lab` in benchmark-lab follow-up; stamp labels will be ingested into results artifacts for attribution.
